title: AI scientist for Quantum Computing (Massy)
description:
About Quandela:

Quandela is a European deeptech company building modular, scalable and energy-efficient spin-photonic quantum computers.

We develop the full quantum computing stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic processors to control systems, software and applications. Our platforms are available through the cloud and as on-premises systems.

Our ambition is to build fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of classical computation.

The role:

We are looking for an AI Scientist to join Quandela’s AI and Quantum Machine Learning team in Massy (near Paris)

You will develop and evaluate machine-learning approaches for quantum computing, covering both:

- AI for quantum systems, including calibration, control, decoding for quantum error correction;
- quantum and hybrid machine learning, including rigorous comparisons with state-of-the-art classical methods, using MerLin, Quandela's framework for quantum machine learning.

You will work on research with colleagues across AI, quantum algorithms, software, product and hardware.

The Massy team is a central part of Quandela’s AI activities. This role therefore offers significant ownership and the opportunity to help shape and grow the team over time.

What You'll Do:

- Design, implement and train machine-learning and quantum machine-learning models.
- Develop AI methods to improve the calibration, control and performance of quantum systems.
- Benchmark classical, quantum and hybrid methods using meaningful baselines and evaluation metrics.
- Contribute actively to the development of the MerLin framework.
- Contribute to publications and collaborations with academic partners, including research ecosystem.
- Present your work internally and at scientific conferences and technical events.
- Help define Quandela’s future AI research directions and mentor junior researchers as the team grows.

Requirements

What we are looking for:

We are looking for an AI scientist, or an experienced industry practitioner with an equivalent background, who is eager to apply state-of-the-art classical machine-learning methods to scientific and engineering challenges in quantum computing. The role is primarily focused on using AI to improve quantum technologies, while also providing opportunities to develop and investigate quantum and hybrid machine-learning models.

- PhD + 3 years of experience or equivalent industrial R&D experience in machine learning.
- Strong foundations in modern machine learning, experimental methodology and model evaluation.
- Excellent scientific programming skills, particularly in Python and common machine-learning frameworks.
- Experience taking research ideas from initial exploration to robust implementation.
- Interest in working on both longer term research and concrete product problems.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work autonomously within a focused, multidisciplinary team.
- Professional fluency in English.

Bonus Points

- Previous experience applying AI to physical systems, scientific computing, hardware control or experimental data.
- Knowledge of quantum computing, quantum machine learning or photonic quantum technologies.
- Experience mentoring junior researchers or helping define technical research directions.

Benefits

- Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience and expectations

- Profit-sharing & company savings plan
- 100% health coverage (Alan)
- 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
- Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
- Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

Process:

- Talent Acquisition Interview (30' - 45')
- Hiring Manager Interview (45' - 60')
- Reference checks
- Technical discussion and presentation of previous research work
- Meeting with the team
- Offer

Beyond That:
At Quandela, we value scientific curiosity, experimentation and collaboration. If you're passionate about quantum optics, spin physics and quantum technologies, we'd love to hear from you, even if you don't meet every listed requirement.

If you're excited by the challenge of turning scientific ideas into demonstrations, advancing the building blocks of future quantum computing systems and working alongside physicists, engineers and theorists, let's talk.

title: Chief of Staff - Schwerpunkt Fördermittel & Akademische Partnerschaften

title: Fiber Integration Engineer (PhD level)
description:
Quandela stands as a global leader in quantum computing, driven by groundbreaking technology and a strategic vision for scaling quantum solutions. The company’s unique ability to offer both hardware and software solutions, along with its commitment to build energy efficient quantum processing units that scale, positions it to play a key role in the next wave of innovation, and in many strategic and sovereign industrial sectors.

With a team of more than 140 people, we develop our own hardware and software stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic processors to quantum control systems and quantum algorithms.

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of classical computation using Quandela's cutting-edge quantum dot technology.

Achieving this vision requires not only advances in photonic quantum computing, but also the development of scalable spin-photon interfaces, distributed entanglement capabilities and future SPOQC (Spin-Optical Quantum Computing) architectures that will enable modular and fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀

About this position:

Join Quandela’s Source Production team to work on the fiber pigtailing of single-photon sources.
The role focuses on developing, improving and operating highly precise fiber coupling methods for photonic quantum devices.

The role is part of the Source Production team, which currently includes 11 people across fabrication, fiber pigtailing and optical characterization. The role is part of the pigtail team, currently composed of one person, and works in close interaction with the fabrication and characterization teams.

The objective is to improve the reliability, reproducibility and productivity of the pigtailing process, from prototype development to production-ready methods.

Key responsibilities

- Integrating mircro-structure to the PIC waveguide edge coupling

- Perform high-precision fiber coupling between single-mode fibers and individual micropillars, with alignment precision below 100 nm
- Develop and improve methods to evaluate coupling and alignment quality through clear metrics
- Cool down pigtailed sources and support the validation of the assembled devices
- Perform optical characterization of quantum emitters using quantum optics techniques, including single-photon detection
- Contribute to the development of reliable and reproducible production procedures
- Write systematic reports and share production feedback with other teams
- Work closely with the fabrication and optical characterization teams
- Contribute to productivity improvements and risk mitigation in the pigtailing process
- Simulation experience is a plus

Requirements

Desired profile

Required

- PhD or engineering degree in optics, photonics, optomechanics, experimental physics or a related field
- Strong hands-on experience in optics and optical alignment
- Experience with fiber coupling, fiber handling or fiber-based optical systems
- Good understanding of photonic structures and optical components
- Experience with cryogenic systems or low-temperature optical setups
- Ability to work with high precision and follow established procedures
- Good communication and reporting skills
- Good level of English

Nice to have

- Experience with quantum emitters or single-photon sources
- Simulation experience is a plus
- Good balance between hands-on and simulation, ideally around 70% hands-on / 30% simulation

Soft skills

- Very precise and rigorous
- Strong respect for procedures
- Creative when developing new methods
- Reliable and methodical
- Good risk mitigation mindset
- Team player
- Hands-on and practical

title: Quantum Algorithms & Resource Estimation Scientist
description:
- About Quandela:

Quandela is a European deeptech scale-up building modular, scalable, energy-efficient photonic and spin-optical quantum computers.

Our quantum computing platform is accessible both via the cloud and on-premises.

With a team of more than 140 people, we develop the entire quantum computing stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic processors to quantum control systems and algorithms.

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of classical computation.

Achieving this vision requires continuous advances across the full stack, including the design, evaluation and practical application of next-generation quantum algorithms for both today's quantum platforms and tomorrow's fault-tolerant systems.

- About this position:

For this position, you will join the ALPS (Algorithms & Applications) team, where quantum algorithms, applications and hardware architectures come together to explore how quantum computing can create long-term scientific and industrial value across a broad range of application domains.

Working closely with colleagues across the Quantum Acceleration Program, as well as with Quandela's Quantum Information, FTQC, Software and Hardware teams, you will contribute to collaborative R&D projects alongside leading academic, institutional and industrial partners.

Your work will focus on evaluating advanced algorithmic approaches beyond the NISQ era, with a particular emphasis on fault-tolerant quantum algorithms, modern algorithmic primitives and resource estimation.

You will assess the feasibility, scalability and implementation costs of these approaches for Quandela's spin-photonic quantum computing architecture, helping shape future technology roadmaps.

- What You'll Do:

As a Quantum Algorithms & Resource Estimation Scientist, you will contribute to the evaluation, adaptation and practical assessment of advanced fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for future large-scale photonic quantum computers.

Your work will include:

- Explore and evaluate fault-tolerant quantum algorithms and modern algorithmic primitives.
- Study approaches such as Block-Encoding, QSP, QSVT and Hamiltonian Simulation.
- Perform resource estimation studies to assess feasibility, scalability and resources.
- Adapt quantum algorithms to Quandela's spin-photonic QC architecture.
- Collaborate with FTQC, Quantum Information and Architecture teams.
- Contribute to collaborative R&D projects with academic and industrial partners.
- Monitor advances in FTQC algorithms and resource estimation methodologies.
- Communicate research through reports, publications, conferences

- How You Will Grow?

First 3 months:
Develop a solid understanding of Quandela's spin-photonic QC architecture, the FTQC roadmap and the objectives of the Quantum Acceleration Program.
Contribute to your first research project, building hands-on experience in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms and resource estimation.

Within 6 months:
Take ownership of your project and contribute independently to algorithm evaluation and resource estimation studies.
Broaden your involvement across additional research activities within the ALPS team while building strong collaborations throughout the Quantum Acceleration Program.

Within 1 year:
Become a key contributor to Quandela's long-term research on fault-tolerant QC.
Drive collaborative R&D initiatives across Quantum Information, FTQC, Software and Architecture teams.
Contribute to Quandela's scientific visibility through publications, conferences and technical exchanges.

Requirements

- Ideal Profile:

We are looking for a scientist or engineer with a strong theoretical background in quantum algorithms and fault-tolerant quantum computing. You enjoy bridging advanced algorithmic research with practical questions around scalability, implementation and future quantum computing architectures.

- PhD or Postdoctoral research experience in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Quantum Information, Quantum Computing or a closely related field.
- Experience with modern fault-tolerant algorithmic primitives and frameworks, such as Block-Encoding, QSP, QSVT, Qubitization, Hamiltonian Simulation or related approaches.

- Experience communicating scientific results through publications, conferences or technical presentations.
- Familiarity with photonic quantum computing or photonic quantum architectures is appreciated but not required.

- Hiring Manager Interviews (45' - 60')
- Reference checks

At Quandela, we value intellectual diversity, curiosity and initiative. If you're passionate about quantum algorithms, fault-tolerant quantum computing and the future of large-scale quantum applications, we'd love to hear from you, even if you don't meet every listed requirement.

title: Quantum Information Scientist - Architecture & Performance
description:
About Quandela:

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers.
Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving problems beyond the reach of classical computation.

Getting there will require several generations of intermediate architectures. Choosing the right ones means understanding what can be built, what these systems can compute and how efficiently they can do so.

About this position:

You will join Quandela’s Quantum Information team within Architecture, working on the evaluation and design of our near- and mid-term quantum architectures.

Your role will sit between quantum theory, computational capability and real hardware constraints. You will develop methods to evaluate architecture concepts, understand their performance and limitations, and help guide future architecture choices.

Depending on your background, you may draw on complexity theory, quantum learning theory, quantum-system characterisation, benchmarking or related areas. You will work closely with our Device Physics, FTQC and Q.Algorithms Team.

Requirements

What you'll do:

As a Quantum Information Scientist working on Architecture & Performance, you will:

- Evaluate and compare the capabilities and limitations of near- and mid-term quantum architectures.
- Draw on methods from complexity theory, benchmarking, characterisation and related fields to assess different architecture designs.
- Incorporate realistic noise, native operations and physical constraints into your analyses.
- Investigate when and how different architectures could provide meaningful computational capabilities or advantages.
- Develop scientific models and numerical tools to explore architecture-performance trade-offs.
- Study how architecture choices interact with algorithms, resource requirements and QEC strategies.
- Progressively propose and lead new research projects around architecture design and performance.

You will work across our Architecture team and Algorithms and Applications team, connecting questions from the physical layer to computational capability and potential applications.
- How you'll grow:

During your first 3–6 months
Become familiar with Quandela’s technologies, architecture roadmap and ongoing research while contributing to existing evaluation and performance studies.

Within 1 year
Take increasing ownership of architecture studies, compare different concepts and bring your own scientific perspective to the team.

Longer term
Lead exploratory research projects, propose new architecture directions and contribute to shaping Quandela’s future architecture roadmap.

--

What we're looking for:
We are looking for a scientist with a strong theoretical background in quantum computing, scientific autonomy and an interest in connecting different layers of the quantum-computing stack.

Must-have

- PhD in Quantum Information, Quantum Computing, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a closely related field.
- Strong expertise in one or more relevant areas, such as quantum complexity theory, quantum learning theory, quantum-system characterisation, performance analysis or quantum algorithms.
- Experience connecting theoretical or computational questions with realistic implementation, hardware or experimental constraints.
- Ability to assess the capabilities and limitations of quantum systems or architectures.
- Experience with scientific modelling, numerical simulation and Python-based scientific computing.
- Scientific autonomy and ability to structure open-ended research problems.
- Collaborative and personable, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly to people from other fields of expertise.
- Professional English.

Important, but you can grow here

- Quantum Error Correction and early fault-tolerant architectures.
- Hardware-aware algorithm or architecture design.
- Quantum benchmarking and performance metrics.
- Noise modelling.
- Resource and computational-cost analysis.
- Collaboration with experimental or hardware-oriented quantum-computing teams.

Bonus

- Quantum compilation or native-gate-aware circuit design.
- Photonic quantum computing.
- Resource estimation.
- Experience comparing quantum approaches against strong classical baselines.
- Previous ownership of collaborative research projects.

You do not need to cover every topic above. We welcome both candidates with postdoctoral or equivalent industrial R&D experience and strong recent PhDs demonstrating scientific autonomy.

Benefits

Join a growing quantum-computing company and contribute directly to the research behind future generations of quantum architectures.

- Explore open scientific questions grounded in real hardware constraints.
- Work across Quantum Information, Device Physics, FTQC and Algorithms.
- Take ownership of broad and exploratory research projects.
- Contribute to the scientific directions of a growing team.

Plus:

- Competitive compensation aligned with your experience and level of responsibility.
- Company savings plan.
- 100% health coverage through Alan.
- Transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus.
- Swile meal vouchers.
- Access to Gymlib.

Process

- Talent Acquisition interview, 30–45 min
- Interview with Quantum Information hiring manager, 30-45 min
- Presentation of previous research work and discussion with members of the theory team
- Reference checks
- Technical discussion based on a scientific paper or research topic
- Offer

For the technical exercise, you may be asked to explore scientific material outside your direct area of expertise and discuss how you would connect it to a broader architecture problem.

title: Quantum Information Scientist - Quantum Dot Modelling
description:
About Quandela:

Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges.
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers.
Within Scalable Architecture, we model the physical systems behind our technologies to understand their limitations and guide future designs.

About this position:

You will join our Device Physics team, which develops theoretical and numerical models of Quandela’s physical systems in close interaction with experimental teams.

You will focus on quantum dots and their phononic environment, modelling how phonon-induced noise affects our semiconductor photon sources.

Your work will range from calculating phonon spectral densities to integrating these effects into existing source models. The scientific problem and possible approaches are already identified, giving you a strong foundation from which to progressively take ownership of the topic.

- What you'll do:

As a Quantum Information Scientist working on Quantum Dot Modelling, you will:

- Develop numerical models of quantum dot-phonon interactions and phonon-induced noise.
- Calculate relevant physical quantities, including phonon spectral densities, and integrate them into existing source models.
- Apply finite-element, finite-difference and related numerical methods to semiconductor nanostructures.
- Build and run simulations using COMSOL Multiphysics or comparable simulation platforms.
- Validate your models against physical expectations, existing models and experimental results.
- Develop scientific code primarily in Python, with opportunities to move toward C++ for more demanding simulations.
- Use validated models to explore possible improvements in photon-source design and operation.

- How you'll grow:

During your first months: Become familiar with Quandela’s quantum-dot systems and develop your first phonon simulations with support from Device Physics and experimental teams.

Within 6–12 months: integrate and validate your work within our wider modelling framework and take increasing ownership of the topic.

Longer term: Explore optimisation strategies, additional physical effects and new research directions around semiconductor quantum systems.

Requirements

What we're looking for:

We are looking for a scientist combining strong physical understanding with hands-on numerical modelling experience, ideally in semiconductor, condensed-matter or computational physics.

Direct quantum-computing experience is not required. What matters is your ability to translate a physical problem into a credible numerical model and critically assess its results.

Must-have:

- Master’s or PhD in Physics, Photonics, Semiconductor Physics, Condensed Matter Physics, Computational Physics or a closely related field.
- Strong foundations in semiconductor, condensed-matter or related quantum physics.
- Hands-on experience modelling physical systems numerically.
- Experience with FEM, finite-difference or related numerical methods, ideally using COMSOL Multiphysics or comparable simulation tools.
- Python for scientific modelling and data analysis.
- Ability to understand the physics behind a simulation, challenge its assumptions and validate its results.
- Ability to collaborate with both theoretical and experimental researchers.
- Professional English.

Important, but you can grow here:

- Quantum-dot or semiconductor nanostructure modelling.
- Phonon physics and phonon-induced noise.
- Experience with multiphysics or electromagnetic simulation tools, including Ansys or Lumerical.
- C++ for scientific computing.
- Scientific or quantum-modelling packages such as QuTip.

Bonus:

- Phonon engineering.
- Modelling of charge, nuclear-spin or other semiconductor noise mechanisms.
- Experience connecting numerical models with experimental measurements.
- Quantum-information knowledge and an understanding of how physical noise impacts quantum computation.

We are open to strong Master’s-level profiles with substantial hands-on research experience in numerical modelling. You do not need expertise across every layer of the problem.

Benefits

Join a research team where theoretical and numerical work directly feeds into experiments and hardware development.

- Work on a concrete scientific problem connected to Quandela’s semiconductor photon sources.
- Collaborate closely with theorists and experimental physicists.
- Progressively build scientific ownership as your models become part of Quandela’s wider modelling framework.
- Contribute to publications, conferences and new research directions.

Plus:

- Competitive compensation aligned with your experience and level of responsibility.
- Company savings plan.
- 100% health coverage through Alan.
- Transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus.
- Swile meal vouchers.
- Access to Gymlib.

Process

- Talent Acquisition interview, 30–45 min
- Scientific interview with members of the team
- Discussion of your previous research and numerical-modelling experience
- Technical scientific discussion
- Reference checks
- Final discussion with the team
- Offer

The scientific discussions are intended to understand how you approach a physical modelling problem, choose appropriate numerical methods, assess assumptions and connect simulation results with a real physical system.

Beyond that:
If you enjoy using numerical modelling to understand real physical systems and seeing that work feed into experiments, this role offers the opportunity to deepen your expertise in semiconductor quantum systems while progressively taking ownership of the topic.

You’ll work where precision meets performance: at the intersection of quantum optics research and operational hardware.

We are opening a Quantum Optics Scientist position to accelerate the transition from advanced quantum optics experiments to stable, integrated hardware within our QPUs. You’ll help the team scale our systems from research prototypes to operational processors - pushing performance, reproducibility, and stability across the stack.

Your experiments don’t end at the bench : they run inside real quantum computers.
You’ll translate quantum optics into stable, cloud-ready QPU modules.

You’ll help us cross the bridge from experimental setups to robust processors that support feedforward and error correction.
This role defines how quantum theory becomes quantum reality - one module at a time.

- Prototype and operate quantum optics modules

- Code for the lab
Develop pragmatic Python tools for acquisition, calibration, and analysis (scripts, utilities, quick plots) - tools your teammates actually reuse.

As part of the Office of the CTO & CSO, the role provides direct exposure to the executive leadership team (COMEX) and involvement in shaping some of the company’s most strategic technical and scientific decisions.

The position operates at the intersection of research, engineering and product development, helping maintain clarity, alignment and execution discipline as the organization scales.

Impact in the First 12 Months

In this role, you will play a key part in strengthening the execution and coordination of Quandela’s technical and scientific strategy. During your first year, you are expected to:

Build alignment across research, product and engineering

- Develop a strong understanding of Quandela’s scientific and technical roadmap.

- Improve coordination mechanisms between research teams, product leadership and engineering.

Bring structure and visibility to key technical initiatives

- Implement clear tracking and governance for major technical and scientific programs.

- Ensure leadership has visibility on milestones, dependencies and risks.

Strengthen the Office of the CTO & CSO

- Contribute to structuring the operating model of the Office of the CTO & CSO, including leadership rhythms and technical reviews.

- Support preparation and follow-up of key leadership discussions and decision processes.

Accelerate cross-team execution

- Help resolve cross-team challenges impacting critical technical initiatives.

- Improve communication flows and coordination between research, product and engineering teams.

Support the scaling of the technical organization

- Assist the CTO/CPO and CSO in structuring processes and initiatives that allow the organization to scale while maintaining scientific and technical excellence.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Support to Technical Leadership

- Support the CTO/CPO and CSO in structuring and driving Quandela’s technical and scientific priorities.

- Prepare strategic materials, technical briefings and leadership reviews.

- Help synthesize complex technical topics to facilitate decision-making at the leadership level.

Office of the CTO & CSO Operations

- Contribute to the functioning of the Office of the CTO & CSO by structuring leadership processes and coordination mechanisms.

- Support preparation and follow-up of technical leadership meetings, reviews and strategic discussions.

- Help maintain alignment across research, engineering and product leadership.

Program Governance & Coordination

- Track progress on key technical and scientific initiatives across the organization.

- Ensure visibility on milestones, dependencies and risks.

- Facilitate coordination between teams and support resolution of cross-team blockers.

Organizational Effectiveness (P1)

- Improve internal processes supporting technical and research operations.

- Structure communication flows between research teams and product and engineering teams

- Ensure structuration of the teams

- Help maintain alignment between scientific exploration and product development priorities.

Strategic Projects

- Lead or coordinate high-impact cross-functional initiatives on behalf of the CTO/CPO and CSO.

- Provide analytical and operational support on complex organizational or technical topics.

Requirements

Who Thrives in This Role

This role is ideal for individuals who enjoy operating at the intersection of advanced science, engineering execution and strategic coordination.

You will thrive in this position if you:

- Are comfortable navigating highly technical environments and interacting with leading scientists and engineers.

- Enjoy structuring complex problems and bringing clarity to ambiguous situations.

- Have a strong bias for execution and impact, with the ability to move initiatives forward across teams.

- Are able to earn trust quickly with senior technical leaders through rigor, discretion and sound judgment.

- Are motivated by the opportunity to contribute to the development of cutting-edge scientific and technological programs.

Profile

Experience

5+ years of experience in roles such as:

- Chief of Staff

- Technical Program Manager

- Strategy / operations in deeptech organizations

- Technology consulting

Experience working in research-driven environments, advanced technology companies, or deeptech startups is strongly preferred.

Education

- Advanced degree (MSc or PhD) in physics, computer science or a related technical field is required.

- A dual background combining engineering/science and business, management or project management (e.g. engineering degree plus business school, MBA, or equivalent training) is a strong plus.

Skills

- Exceptional structuring and synthesis capabilities

- Strong program and project coordination skills

- Ability to engage effectively with senior scientists and engineers

- Excellent written and verbal communication

- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities

Personal Qualities

- Highly organized and proactive

- Strong sense of ownership and discretion

- Comfortable operating in highly technical environments

- Ability to navigate complex organizations and evolving priorities

Benefits

Joining Quandela means contributing to the development of one of Europe’s leading quantum computing companies, at the frontier of photonic quantum technologies.

As part of the Office of the CTO & CSO, this role offers a unique opportunity to work at the center of the company’s scientific and technical leadership, gaining direct exposure to strategic decisions and helping shape the execution of cutting-edge research and engineering programs.

You will collaborate with world-class scientists and engineers while helping scale a fast-growing deeptech organization tackling some of the most challenging technological problems of our time.

title: Technicien Polyvalent Maintenance, Logistique & Services Généraux
description:
Quandela est un leader mondial de l'informatique quantique : l'entreprise conçoit, fabrique et fournit des solutions quantiques de pointe pour la recherche et l'industrie. Son offre comprend les ordinateurs quantiques les plus économes en énergie pour les centres de données, des solutions d'informatique quantique full-stack accessibles via le cloud, ainsi que des services d'accès à des algorithmes pour les clients académiques et industriels. Suivant une feuille de route pragmatique et progressive, Quandela déploie depuis 2023 des systèmes de qualité industrielle, tout en développant les futures générations d'ordinateurs quantiques tolérants aux fautes, capables de passer à l'échelle grâce à l'intégration de milliers de composants photoniques. Quandela s'engage à rendre l'informatique quantique accessible à tous afin de relever les défis industriels et sociétaux les plus complexes.

Rejoignez-nous à l'avant-garde de l'innovation en informatique quantique 🚀

Vous aimez le travail concret, varié et utile ?

Nous recherchons un.e technicien.e polyvalent.e expérimenté.e pour rejoindre notre équipe, à temps partiel (4 jours/semaine)

Au quotidien, vous contribuerez au bon fonctionnement de nos locaux et apporterez un soutien aux équipes à travers des missions variées.

Entretien et petits travaux

- Réaliser de petits travaux de bricolage et d'aménagement (montage de meubles, réparations simples, petites installations, ...).
- Veiller au bon état des locaux et répondre à toute demande nécessitant votre intervention pour dépanner, réparer le plus rapidement et efficacement possible.
- Effectuer quelques vérifications régulières pour s'assurer que tout fonctionne correctement.

Logistique

- Réceptionner, contrôler et ranger les livraisons (ce n'est pas de la supply chain, un colis par-ci, par-là)
- Préparer le matériel nécessaire pour les démonstrations, salons et autres événements.

Soutien aux équipes

- Participer ponctuellement au montage et à la préparation de certains équipements.
- Donner un coup de main aux différentes équipes lorsque cela est nécessaire afin d'assurer le bon déroulement des activités.
- De manière ponctuelle, livrer du matériel entre le site de Massy et celui de Palaiseau

Requirements

Nous recherchons avant tout une personne fiable, débrouillarde et pragmatique.

Votre expérience de terrain, votre bon sens et votre capacité à résoudre des problèmes concrets auront bien plus de valeur qu'un diplôme spécifique.

Vous vous reconnaissez si :

- Vous aimez le travail manuel et les missions variées ;
- Vous êtes autonome et savez organiser votre travail ;
- Vous trouvez naturellement des solutions pratiques face aux imprévus ;
- Vous aimez rendre service et travailler en équipe ;
- Vous avez une expérience dans la maintenance, les services généraux, la logistique, le bâtiment ou tout autre métier technique.

Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, technique ou logistique est un plus, mais ce sont avant tout votre savoir-faire, votre expérience et votre envie de contribuer qui feront la différence.

Nous accueillons avec intérêt les candidatures de professionnels expérimentés, notamment celles de personnes souhaitant poursuivre leur activité en mettant leur expertise au service d'une entreprise innovante et en pleine croissance.

Benefits

- Dispositifs de participation et d'épargne salariale.

- Prise en charge à 100 % de votre couverture santé (Alan).

- Remboursement à 50 % de votre abonnement aux transports en commun ou forfait mobilité durable.

- Titres-restaurant (Swile) et participation à un abonnement sportif via Gymlib.

- Aides à la parentalité et prime de cooptation comprise entre 1 000 € et 2 000 €.

L'environnement de travail :

- Culture d'entreprise stimulante et innovante
- Équipes passionnées et multiculturelles
- Opportunités de participer à des événements internationaux dans le domaine quantique
- Sentiment d'appartenance à un projet pionnier européen dans les technologies quantiques

Process

- Echange avec Sandrine Talent Partner (30')
- Echange sur site avec ton futur manager Samuel (45')
- 1 prise de référence
- Offre - bienvenue à bord !

Rejoindre Quandela comme technicien logistique, c'est devenir un maillon essentiel dans le déploiement de la plus puissante technologie d'informatique quantique photonique au monde!
